# Agentic ODI 🚀

[![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**

## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation

**Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis.

**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. 

The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes.

## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed)

This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery.

### Code Overview

This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of five installable projects, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests:

- **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`): Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation.
- **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`): A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value).
- **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`): A local FastAPI server that talks to the repository directly (no MCP transport).
- **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`): A Python-based agent client that communicates with the MCP server, executing tool calls over the active connection. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Streamlit UI together.
- **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`): A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides a non-MCP entry point for interacting with Agentic ODI, initially exposing `--version` and `--help`, and will grow to cover dataset operations.

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Prerequisites

Python 3.10+ and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Install the whole workspace (all five projects plus dev tooling):

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, and `agentic-odi-cli` in editable mode.

### Running the Environment

#### 🧰 Command-line interface (CLI)

Agentic ODI ships a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI so you can interact with the project directly from your terminal — no MCP client or chat UI required. Today it provides version and help information; over time it will expose commands for working with the ODI dataset (Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes), giving you a scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to the MCP/chat path.

Launch it with:

```bash
python -m cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
python -m cli --help      # show available options and commands
python -m cli             # show help when no command is given
```

A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.

#### Manage Customer Outcomes

Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`):

```bash
# Add a Customer Outcome
agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors"   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding"   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2   --category cost_reduction   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"

# List outcomes (optionally filtered)
agentic-odi outcomes list
agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id <job-id>

# Get, update, delete
agentic-odi outcomes get <outcome-id>
agentic-odi outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
agentic-odi outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes

# Compute ODI Opportunity Score
agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
```

Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed.


After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

### 🧠 Superpowers with Pi

This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded.

To enable:

1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`
2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve`
3. Start Pi: `pi`

The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi will clone it and load:

- **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and after compaction
- **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development, systematic-debugging, etc.)

> [!NOTE]
> Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`. The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode compatibility layer.

### 🧼 Developer workflow for formatting

- **When editing Python files**, either:
  - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or
  - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing:

    ```bash
    uv run ruff format .
    ```

- **CI behavior**:
  - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files.
  - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only.
  - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again.

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `core/tests/test_models.py` | Domain models and ODI opportunity-score computation |
| `core/tests/test_service.py` | `ODIService` jobs/steps/outcomes and Customer Outcome CRUD |
| `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool |
| `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation |
| `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools |
| `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` |
| `local_server/tests/test_api.py` | Local FastAPI health endpoint |
| `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks) |
| `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior |
| `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI subcommands with MCP stub |

**Conventions:**
- Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named `test_*.py`.
- Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
- Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests.
- The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test.

> [!TIP]
> Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically.

## ☁️ Deployment

The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.

### 🧪 Test Chat (UI)

Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:

> **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)**

### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint

Integrate via the MCP protocol at:

> **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client.

---

## 🗺️ Roadmap & Next Steps

As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include:

- [ ] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*, *Steps*, and *Outcomes*.
- [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `cli/` so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path.
- [ ] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like `get_job_map(job_id)` or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`.
- [ ] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the fastmcp server to a lightweight vector or relational database containing actual user research data.
- [ ] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the client up to an LLM (e.g., via LangChain or standard OpenAI clients) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features.

---

*Let's build AI that builds what people actually need.*

## 🏗️ Architecture

This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) composed of five installable packages, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests:

| Package | Purpose | Key Technologies |
|---|---|---|
| **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, `ODIService` business logic, and repository implementations (in-memory/SQLite). Includes ODI opportunity score computation. | Pydantic, SQLModel |
| **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | MCP server exposing HTTP transport. Hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes. | [FastMCP](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) |
| **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | Local FastAPI server that interfaces directly with repositories (no MCP transport layer). | FastAPI, Uvicorn |
| **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | Python agent client for MCP server communication with tool execution. Includes `run.py` for local dev (server + Streamlit UI). | FastMCP Client, Streamlit |
| **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | Typer-based CLI for terminal interaction with Agentic ODI - scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to MCP/chat. | [Typer](https://github.com/fastapi/typer) |

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Python **3.10+**
- [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager

### Installation

Install the entire workspace (all five projects plus dev tooling):

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, and `agentic-odi-cli` in editable mode.

---

## 💻 Usage

### Command-Line Interface (CLI)

The Typer-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal—no MCP client or chat UI required.

```bash
# Version and help
python -m cli --version   # Print the Agentic ODI version
python -m cli --help      # Show available options and commands
python -m cli             # Show help when no command is given

# Console script also works
agentic-odi --version
```

### Managing Customer Outcomes

Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the MCP server must be running:

```bash
# Start the MCP server (in a separate terminal)
python -m mcp_server
```

Then use the CLI to manage outcomes:

```bash
# Add a Customer Outcome
agentic-odi outcomes add \
  --job-id <job-id> \
  --direction minimize \
  --unit "time" \
  --object "to resolve setup errors" \
  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
  --importance 8.8 \
  --satisfaction 3.2 \
  --category cost_reduction \
  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"

# List outcomes (optionally filtered)
agentic-odi outcomes list
agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id <job-id>

# Get, update, delete
agentic-odi outcomes get <outcome-id>
agentic-odi outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
agentic-odi outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes

# Compute ODI Opportunity Score
agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
```

> **Tip:** Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed.
EOF

| **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | Python agent client for MCP server communication with tool execution. Includes `run.py` for local dev (server + Streamlit UI). | FastMCP Client, Streamlit |
| **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | Typer-based CLI for terminal interaction with Agentic ODI - scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to MCP/chat. | [Typer](https://github.com/fastapi/typer) |

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Python **3.10+**
- [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager

### Installation

Install the entire workspace (all five projects plus dev tooling):

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, and `agentic-odi-cli` in editable mode.

---

## 💻 Usage

### Command-Line Interface (CLI)

The Typer-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal—no MCP client or chat UI required.

```bash
# Version and help
python -m cli --version   # Print the Agentic ODI version
python -m cli --help      # Show available options and commands
python -m cli             # Show help when no command is given

# Console script also works
agentic-odi --version
```

### Managing Customer Outcomes

Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the MCP server must be running:

```bash
# Start the MCP server (in a separate terminal)
python -m mcp_server
```

Then use the CLI to manage outcomes:

```bash
# Add a Customer Outcome
agentic-odi outcomes add \
  --job-id <job-id> \
  --direction minimize \
  --unit "time" \
  --object "to resolve setup errors" \
  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
  --importance 8.8 \
  --satisfaction 3.2 \
  --category cost_reduction \
  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"

# List outcomes (optionally filtered)
agentic-odi outcomes list
agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id <job-id>

# Get, update, delete
agentic-odi outcomes get <outcome-id>
agentic-odi outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
agentic-odi outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes

# Compute ODI Opportunity Score
agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
```

> **Tip:** Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed.
EOF

```bash
uv run pytest

uv run pytest --cov
```

### Local tools-capable LLM backend (for MCP testing)

To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that:

- Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and
- Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**.

A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server.

1. **Install a local LLM server**

   Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes):

   ```bash
   pip install llama-cpp-python
   ```

2. **Download a small tools-capable model**

   Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`.

3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server**

   Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`):

   ```bash
   python -m llama_cpp.server \
     --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \
     --model_alias local-tools-model \
     --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
     --chat_format openai
   ```

   This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`.

4. **Point the Streamlit client at the local server**

   `client/src/client/app.py` reads defaults from environment variables (with sensible fallbacks):

   - `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8001/v1`)
   - `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` (default: `local`)
   - `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` (default: `local-tools-model`)
   - `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`)

   You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **“LLM Configuration”**.

5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server**

   - (Optional) Before starting the UI, you can quickly verify that the LLM backend is reachable:

     ```bash
     curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models
     ```

     If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server.

   - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above).
   - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: “Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository.”
   - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together.
   - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup.

#### 🤖 Agent-driven testing

Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results.

## 🧪 Testing

Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact:

```bash
uv run --directory core pytest
uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
uv run --directory local_server pytest
uv run --directory client pytest
uv run --directory cli pytest
```

### 🧠 Agent session tracking

Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints.

### 🧹 Linting, formatting & type checks (CI parity)

The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with:

```bash
# Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml)
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .

uv run --directory core mypy .
uv run --directory mcp_server mypy .
uv run --directory local_server mypy .
uv run --directory client mypy .
uv run --directory cli mypy .

# Security scanning
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src

# Tests (same as CI)
uv run --directory core pytest
uv run --directory mcp_server pytest
uv run --directory local_server pytest
uv run --directory client pytest
uv run --directory cli pytest
```

To run these automatically before each commit, you can enable the bundled pre-commit hooks:

```bash
uv tool install pre-commit
pre-commit install
```

After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with:

```bash
pre-commit run --all-files
```

This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded.

To enable:

1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh`
2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve`
3. Start Pi: `pi`

The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi will clone it and load:

- **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and after compaction
- **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development, systematic-debugging, etc.)

> [!NOTE]
> Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`. The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode compatibility layer.

# Agentic ODI 🚀

[![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**

## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation

**Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis.

**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. 

The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes.

## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed)

This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery.

### Code Overview

This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of five installable projects, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests:

- **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`): Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation.
- **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`): A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value).
- **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`): A local FastAPI server that talks to the repository directly (no MCP transport).
- **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`): A Python-based agent client that communicates with the MCP server, executing tool calls over the active connection. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Streamlit UI together.
- **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`): A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides a non-MCP entry point for interacting with Agentic ODI, initially exposing `--version` and `--help`, and will grow to cover dataset operations.

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Prerequisites

Python 3.10+ and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Install the whole workspace (all five projects plus dev tooling):

```bash
uv sync --all-packages
```

This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, and `agentic-odi-cli` in editable mode.

### Running the Environment

#### 🧰 Command-line interface (CLI)

Agentic ODI ships a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI so you can interact with the project directly from your terminal — no MCP client or chat UI required. Today it provides version and help information; over time it will expose commands for working with the ODI dataset (Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes), giving you a scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to the MCP/chat path.

Launch it with:

```bash
python -m cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
python -m cli --help      # show available options and commands
python -m cli             # show help when no command is given
```

A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.

#### Manage Customer Outcomes

Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`):

```bash
# Add a Customer Outcome
agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors"   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding"   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2   --category cost_reduction   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"

# List outcomes (optionally filtered)
agentic-odi outcomes list
```

```bash
# Agentic ODI [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- ## 📋 Table of Contents - [The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation](#-the-vision-context-aware-innovation) - [Current State (Experimental Testbed)](#-current-state-experimental-testbed) - [Code Overview](#-code-overview) - [Getting Started](#-getting-started) - [Prerequisites](#prerequisites) - [Command-Line Interface (CLI)](#-command-line-interface-cli) - [Manage Customer Outcomes](#-manage-customer-outcomes) - [One-Command Launch (recommended)](#-one-command-launch-recommended) - [Manual Split-Terminal (alternative)](#-manual-split-terminal-alternative) - [Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend](#-local-tools-capable-llm-backend-for-mcp-testing) - [Testing](#-testing) - [Agent Session Tracking](#-agent-session-tracking) - [Linting, Formatting & Type Checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) - [Superpowers with Pi](#-superpowers-with-pi) - [Developer Workflow for Formatting](#-developer-workflow-for-formatting) - [Deployment](#-deployment) - [Roadmap & Next Steps](#-roadmap--next-steps) - [Contributing](#-contributing) - [License](#-license) --- ## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation **Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis. **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes. --- ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed) This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery. --- ## 🧩 Code Overview This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of five installable projects, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value). | | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | A local FastAPI server that talks to the repository directly (no MCP transport). | | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | A Python-based agent client that communicates with the MCP server, executing tool calls over the active connection. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Streamlit UI together. | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides a non-MCP entry point for interacting with Agentic ODI, initially exposing `--version` and `--help`, and will grow to cover dataset operations. | --- ## 🚀 Getting Started ### Prerequisites - **Python** 3.10+ - [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager Install the entire workspace (all five projects plus dev tooling): ```bash uv sync --all-packages ``` This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, and `agentic-odi-cli` in editable mode. ### 🖥️ Command-Line Interface (CLI) The [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal — no MCP client or chat UI required. Today it provides version and help information; over time it will expose commands for working with the ODI dataset (Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes), giving you a scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to the MCP/chat path. ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # show help when no command is given ``` A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way. ### 📊 Manage Customer Outcomes Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`): ```bash # Add a Customer Outcome agentic-odi outcomes add \ --job-id \ --direction minimize \ --unit "time" \ --object "to resolve setup errors" \ --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \ --importance 8.8 \ --satisfaction 3.2 \ --category cost_reduction \ --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn" # List outcomes (optionally filtered) agentic-odi outcomes list agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id # Get, update, delete agentic-odi outcomes get agentic-odi outcomes update --importance 9.0 agentic-odi outcomes delete --yes # Compute ODI Opportunity Score agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2 ``` > **Tip:** Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed. #### ⚡ One-Command Launch (recommended) `python -m client.run` starts both the MCP server and the Streamlit UI concurrently. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop both. ```bash python -m client.run ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | Streamlit Chat UI | http://localhost:8501 | #### 🔧 Manual Split-Terminal (alternative) Open two terminals and run each process separately: ```bash # Terminal 1 — MCP server python -m mcp_server # Terminal 2 — Streamlit chat UI streamlit run client/src/client/app.py ``` ### 🧠 Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend (for MCP testing) To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**. A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server. 1. **Install a local LLM server** Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes): ```bash pip install llama-cpp-python ``` 2. **Download a small tools-capable model** Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`. 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server** Start the OpenAI-compatible server: ```bash python -m llama_cpp.server --model C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf --host 0.0.0.0 ``` EOF
```

-# Agentic ODI 🚀
-**Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. 
-### Code Overview
-- **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`): Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation.
-- **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`): A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value).
-- **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`): A local FastAPI server that talks to the repository directly (no MCP transport).
-- **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`): A Python-based agent client that communicates with the MCP server, executing tool calls over the active connection. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Streamlit UI together.
-- **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`): A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides a non-MCP entry point for interacting with Agentic ODI, initially exposing `--version` and `--help`, and will grow to cover dataset operations.
-Python 3.10+ and [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Install the whole workspace (all five projects plus dev tooling):
-### Running the Environment
-#### 🧰 Command-line interface (CLI)
-
-Agentic ODI ships a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI so you can interact with the project directly from your terminal — no MCP client or chat UI required. Today it provides version and help information; over time it will expose commands for working with the ODI dataset (Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes), giving you a scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to the MCP/chat path.
-#### Manage Customer Outcomes
-
-
-#### ⚡ One-command launch (recommended)
-#### 🔧 Manual split-terminal (alternative)
-### Local tools-capable LLM backend (for MCP testing)
-4. **Point the Streamlit client at the local server**
-   `client/src/client/app.py` reads defaults from environment variables (with sensible fallbacks):
-   - `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8001/v1`)
-   - `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` (default: `local`)
-   - `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` (default: `local-tools-model`)
-   - `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`)
-   You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **“LLM Configuration”**.
-   - (Optional) Before starting the UI, you can quickly verify that the LLM backend is reachable:
-   - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: “Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository.”
-   - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together.
-   - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup.

-

-# Tests (same as CI)
-To run these automatically before each commit, you can enable the bundled pre-commit hooks:
-```bash
-uv tool install pre-commit
-pre-commit install
-```
-After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with:
-```bash

-```
-### 🧠 Superpowers with Pi
-### 🧼 Developer workflow for formatting
-| File | What it covers |
-|---|---|
-| `core/tests/test_models.py` | Domain models and ODI opportunity-score computation |
-| `core/tests/test_service.py` | `ODIService` jobs/steps/outcomes and Customer Outcome CRUD |
-| `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool |
-| `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation |
-| `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools |
-| `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` |

-| `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks) |
-| `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior |
-| `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI subcommands with MCP stub |

-**Conventions:**

display.text:
# Agentic ODI [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- ## 📋 Table of Contents - [The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation](#-the-vision-context-aware-innovation) - [Current State (Experimental Testbed)](#-current-state-experimental-testbed) - [Code Overview](#-code-overview) - [Getting Started](#-getting-started) - [CLI](#-command-line-interface-cli) - [Manage Customer Outcomes](#-manage-customer-outcomes) - [One-Command Launch](#-one-command-launch-recommended) - [Manual Split-Terminal](#-manual-split-terminal-alternative) - [Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend](#-local-tools-capable-llm-backend-for-mcp-testing) - [Testing](#-testing) - [Agent Session Tracking](#-agent-session-tracking) - [Linting, Formatting & Type Checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) - [Superpowers with Pi](#-superpowers-with-pi) - [Developer Workflow for Formatting](#-developer-workflow-for-formatting) - [Deployment](#️-deployment) - [Roadmap & Next Steps](#️-roadmap--next-steps) - [Contributing](#-contributing) - [License](#-license) --- ## 🌟 The Vision: Context-Aware Innovation **Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)**, built on the "Jobs-to-be-Done" theory, relies on deeply understanding customer needs, desired outcomes, and execution contexts. Historically, applying ODI requires meticulous research, structured data modeling, and rigorous analysis. **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** represents a paradigm shift in how AI systems consume and reason over external context. By adopting MCP, we can bridge the gap between static user research and dynamic, agentic AI. The vision for **Agentic ODI** is to build a unified, open protocol where LLMs and autonomous agents can natively query, understand, and reason over ODI data (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores) dynamically in real-time. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server will act as the "brain" of customer needs, allowing agents to invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions strictly anchored in verified user outcomes. --- ## 🏗️ Current State (Experimental Testbed) This repository serves as an initial sandbox for understanding server-client MCP communication streams. We are utilizing [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) to prototype HTTP-based context delivery. --- ## 🧩 Code Overview This repository is a [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) made up of five installable projects, each with its own `pyproject.toml`, `src/` layout, and tests: | Package | Description | |---|---| | **`core/`** (`agentic-odi-core`) | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, and repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), including ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`mcp_server/`** (`agentic-odi-mcp-server`) | A foundational MCP Server exposing an HTTP transport layer. It hosts tools for Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, and Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value). | | **`local_server/`** (`agentic-odi-local-server`) | A local FastAPI server that talks to the repository directly (no MCP transport). | | **`client/`** (`agentic-odi-client`) | A Python-based agent client that communicates with the MCP server, executing tool calls over the active connection. It also hosts `run.py`, the local dev launcher that starts the server and the Streamlit UI together. | | **`cli/`** (`agentic-odi-cli`) | A [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based command-line interface. It provides a non-MCP entry point for interacting with Agentic ODI, initially exposing `--version` and `--help`, and will grow to cover dataset operations. | --- ## 🚀 Getting Started ### Prerequisites - **Python** 3.10+ - [**uv**](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager Install the entire workspace (all five projects plus dev tooling): ```bash uv sync --all-packages ``` This creates a `.venv` and installs `agentic-odi-core`, `agentic-odi-mcp-server`, `agentic-odi-local-server`, `agentic-odi-client`, and `agentic-odi-cli` in editable mode. ### 💻 Command-Line Interface (CLI) The [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based CLI lets you interact with Agentic ODI directly from your terminal — no MCP client or chat UI required. Today it provides version and help information; over time it will expose commands for working with the ODI dataset (Jobs, Steps, and Outcomes), giving you a scriptable, automation-friendly alternative to the MCP/chat path. Launch it with: ```bash python -m cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m cli --help # show available options and commands python -m cli # show help when no command is given ``` A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way. ### 🎯 Manage Customer Outcomes Manage Customer Outcomes (linking customer value to business value) via the CLI. The CLI acts as an MCP client, so the server must be running (`python -m mcp_server`): ```bash # Add a Customer Outcome agentic-odi outcomes add --job-id --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn" # List outcomes (optionally filtered) agentic-odi outcomes list agentic-odi outcomes list --job-id # Get, update, delete agentic-odi outcomes get agentic-odi outcomes update --importance 9.0 agentic-odi outcomes delete --yes # Compute ODI Opportunity Score agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2 ``` Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` to point to a non-default server if needed. #### ⚡ One-Command Launch (recommended) `python -m client.run` starts both the MCP server and the Streamlit UI concurrently. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop both. ```bash python -m client.run ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | Streamlit Chat UI | http://localhost:8501 | #### 🔧 Manual Split-Terminal (alternative) Open two terminals and run each process separately: ```bash # Terminal 1 — MCP server python -m mcp_server # Terminal 2 — Streamlit chat UI streamlit run client/src/client/app.py ``` ### 🧠 Local Tools-Capable LLM Backend (for MCP testing) To exercise real tool-calling end-to-end against the MCP server, you need a local LLM backend that: - Exposes an **OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API** (for example, `/v1/chat/completions`), and - Supports OpenAI-style **`tools` / `tool_calls`**. A simple fully local option is [`llama-cpp-python`](https://github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python), which can run a quantized model on your machine and expose an OpenAI-compatible server. 1. **Install a local LLM server** Install `llama-cpp-python` in your environment (see its README for platform-specific build notes): ```bash pip install llama-cpp-python ``` 2. **Download a small tools-capable model** Download a small GGUF model that supports function/tool calling (for example, a 7B function-calling variant from Hugging Face) and note its path, e.g. `C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf`. 3. **Start the OpenAI-compatible server** Start the server and give the model a friendly alias that matches the default used by the Streamlit client (`client/src/client/app.py`): ```bash python -m llama_cpp.server \ --model "C:\models\local-tools-model.gguf" \ --model_alias local-tools-model \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \ --chat_format openai ``` This exposes an OpenAI-style API at `http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1`. 4. **Configure the Streamlit client** `client/src/client/app.py` reads the following environment variables (with sensible defaults): | Variable | Default | |---|---| | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | You can either set these in your shell or adjust them in the Streamlit sidebar under **"LLM Configuration"**. 5. **Verify tool-calling against the MCP server** - (Optional) Before starting the UI, confirm the LLM backend is reachable: ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1/models ``` If this request fails, fix your local LLM server configuration before debugging the MCP client/server. - Start the MCP server and Streamlit UI (either via `python -m client.run` or the split-terminal commands above). - In the browser UI, ask the assistant something that should use ODI tools, for example: *"Help me define a new Job-to-be-Done and add it to your ODI repository."* - You should see the assistant briefly display that it is calling tools (for example, `add_job`, `get_jobs`, etc.) and then respond with grounded ODI guidance, confirming that the local LLM, MCP server, and client wiring all work together. - If the LLM backend is unreachable or misconfigured, the UI will show a clear error banner indicating that the backend at your configured **Base URL** could not be reached, along with details from the underlying error. Use that message together with the steps above to fix your local LLM setup. #### 🤖 Agent-Driven Testing Type `/dev` in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it will start both processes, open the browser, send a test message, and report the results. ### 🧹 Linting, Formatting & Type Checks (CI parity) The CI pipeline runs several quality checks. You can mirror them locally with: ```bash # Ruff lint and formatting checks (per-file config comes from each project's pyproject.toml) uv run ruff check . uv run ruff format --check . # Type checking (run per project so each project's config applies) uv run --directory core mypy . uv run --directory mcp_server mypy . uv run --directory local_server mypy . uv run --directory client mypy . uv run --directory cli mypy . # Security scanning uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r core/src mcp_server/src local_server/src cli/src client/src # Tests (same as CI) uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest ``` To run these automatically before each commit, enable the bundled pre-commit hooks: ```bash uv tool install pre-commit pre-commit install ``` After this, `ruff` and `ruff-format` will run on staged files whenever you commit. You can also trigger them manually with: ```bash pre-commit run --all-files ``` ### ✅ Testing Tests use **pytest** with **pytest-asyncio** (strict mode) and run entirely in-memory — no running server required. Each project owns its tests. CI runs the suite on Python **3.10, 3.11, and 3.12** and stores a coverage report as a build artifact: ```bash uv run --directory core pytest uv run --directory mcp_server pytest uv run --directory local_server pytest uv run --directory client pytest uv run --directory cli pytest ``` #### 📊 Test Coverage Map | File | What it covers | |---|---| | `core/tests/test_models.py` | Domain models and ODI opportunity-score computation | | `core/tests/test_service.py` | `ODIService` jobs/steps/outcomes and Customer Outcome CRUD | | `mcp_server/tests/test_odi.py` | Full ODI workflow (add job → steps → outcomes → retrieval) + capabilities tool | | `mcp_server/tests/test_customer_outcomes.py` | Customer Outcomes CRUD, filtering, computed opportunity scores, and tool validation | | `mcp_server/tests/test_server_tools.py` | Error handling and retrieval for the MCP tools | | `mcp_server/tests/test_tools.py` | Tool response-shape contract for `add_job` | | `local_server/tests/test_api.py` | Local FastAPI health endpoint | | `client/tests/test_run.py` | Dev launcher helpers (port checks) | | `cli/tests/test_cli.py` | CLI `--version` and `--help` behavior | | `cli/tests/test_outcomes_cli.py` | Customer Outcomes CLI subcommands with MCP stub | **Conventions:** - Test files live under each project's `tests/` directory and are named `test_*.py`. - Every async test is decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`. - Use `Client(mcp)` directly (no HTTP server needed) for fast, isolated tests. - The server's `reset_db` autouse fixture clears in-memory state before each test. > [!TIP] > Type `/test` in the AI assistant to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically. #### 🧪 Agent Session Tracking Agent sessions are captured with the [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/overview) CLI. The repository integration lives in `.entire/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. Run `entire status` to confirm it is enabled and `entire checkpoint list` to inspect captured checkpoints. ### 🤝 Superpowers with Pi This project includes [Superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers) as a [Pi package](https://pi.dev/docs/packages). When using [Pi](https://pi.dev) with this project, Superpowers skills and extensions are automatically loaded. To enable: 1. Install Pi: `curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh` 2. Trust the project (first time only): `pi config --local --approve` 3. Start Pi: `pi` The `.pi/settings.json` declares the Superpowers package. Pi will clone it and load: - **Extension**: `superpowers.ts` — injects the `using-superpowers` bootstrap at session startup and after compaction - **Skills**: 12 Superpowers skills (TDD, subagent-driven-development, systematic-debugging, etc.) > [!NOTE] > Superpowers is also available for OpenCode via the plugin in `opencode.json`. The Pi package provides native Pi integration without needing the OpenCode compatibility layer. #### 🧼 Developer Workflow for Formatting - **When editing Python files**, either: - Rely on the **pre-commit hooks** above (recommended), or - Run Ruff formatting directly before pushing: ```bash uv run ruff format . ``` - **CI behavior**: - CI runs `uv run ruff check .` to lint without modifying files. - CI runs `uv run ruff format --check .` to *verify* formatting only. - If CI fails on formatting, run `uv run ruff format .` locally, commit the changes, and push again. --- ## ☁️ Deployment The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**, Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents. ### 🧪 Test Chat (UI) Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser: > **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)** ### 🔌 MCP Server Endpoint Integrate via the MCP protocol at: > **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)** > [!IMPORTANT] > **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a client. --- ## 🗺️ Roadmap & Next Steps As we validate the feasibility of this architecture, our next milestones include: - [ ] **ODI Schema Definition**: Define standardized Pydantic models for *Jobs*, *Steps*, and *Outcomes*. - [x] **CLI Dataset Commands**: Extend `cli/` so the ODI dataset can be created, queried, and scored from the terminal, in addition to the current MCP path. - [ ] **Context Tooling**: Replace the dummy `greet` tool with capabilities like `get_job_map(job_id)` or `evaluate_outcome(statement)`. - [ ] **Data Persistence Layer**: Connect the fastmcp server to a lightweight vector or relational database containing actual user research data. - [ ] **Agentic Integration**: Hook the client up to an LLM (e.g., via LangChain or standard OpenAI clients) so the LLM can *discover* the ODI tools and intelligently request customer insights when ideating features. --- ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Please ensure any change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](#-linting-formatting--type-checks-ci-parity) before opening a pull request. --- ## 📄 License No license has been specified for this repository yet. Until one is added, all rights are reserved by the maintainers. Please reach out before reuse or redistribution. ---
*Let's build AI that builds what people actually need.*
